rv.q: At the end of this thrilling and merciless production you leave the theatre feeling both appalled and strangely elated – the sure sign that a tragedy has hit its mark.
Its textures are a mix of ancient and modern. Though it reverberates with a sense of Greek ritual, there's an acute feeling of up-to-dateness.
The play's tragic force emerges strongly and the production's climax seems better suited to modern tastes than Euripides' original.
Ben Power’s adaptation is admirably clear yet I wonder if it underplays the involvement of the ancient Greeks’ gods and man’s alleged helplessness.
Helen McCrory conjures up more a spirit of savage drought, as if she has run out of hope and with it tolerance.
And for us to get to that conclusion is reflective of a quite brilliant production.

cn.t: Critics widely praise this production of Medea, with Helen McCrory's performance drawing particular acclaim for its raw humanity. Carrie Cracknell's modern direction transforms the ancient tragedy into something genuinely disturbing and emotionally devastating.
